   {
    "title": "A callee local's root authority can be handed to the caller through `auths`. The local anchor then escapes, the dead place stays readable and writable after exitFrame, and case 17 is bypassed.",
    "severity": "blocking",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean: TransferPre l.456 `(∀ b ∈ auths, s.Active b ∧ s.frameOf b = placeFrame s.P src)`; NoEscape l.319-320 (judges locality by the holder field `y.frame`, which transferEff rewrites); ExitPre clause 4 l.553-554 `OptP y.origin (…) True` (root authorities are never checked); exitG l.569-572; theorems dependent_cannot_escape_frame l.1794 and exitFrame_releases_all l.1750",
    "cause": "formalization error",
    "evidence": "Spec says:\n- O4: « Une autorité dont l'origine est strictement locale au cadre appelé ne peut pas être rendue persistante dans l'appelant par cette seule opération. »\n- MM-03.3.1: « Un emplacement local ne peut être utilisé après la sortie de son cadre, sauf si une valeur transférable a été légalement déplacée… » and « Un accès temporaire ne peut être prolongé simplement en le stockant dans un cadre plus ancien. »\n- O7 effects: « Fin de validité des emplacements locaux non transférés. »\n- MM-03.3.6: « Une valeur dépendante ne peut être installée dans une destination dont le cadre survivrait à celui d'une ancre locale dont elle dépend. »\n\nLean behaviour. TransferPre accepts in `auths` any active authority held by the source's frame, including the root authority of an unrelated callee local. transferEff then sets that authority's `frame` to the caller frame. From that point:\n- NoEscape (holder frame) treats it as a caller anchor;\n- ExitPre clause 4 skips it because its origin is `none`;\n- exitEff does not release it because its frame is not `f`.\n\nCheck: `cd formal && lake env lean <scratchpad>/review/Fid.lean` checks with no output (all `by decide`).\n\nExample 1. The state f1e is `exitEff (transferEff (write3Eff (write3Eff (enterEff (enterEff S3.init [(none,0)]) [(none,0),(none,0)]) [1]) [2]) 2 0 [1])`. In it:\n- `¬ f1e.Usable 1`;\n- `f1e.Active 1 ∧ f1e.frameOf 1 = some 1`;\n- `Read3Step 1 [1] f1e (.ok f1e)`;\n- `Write3Step 1 [1] f1e (.ok …)`;\n- `Reachable K0 (write3Eff f1e [1])` is proved.\nSo the caller reads and writes leaf 1, which belongs to a local of the exited callee that was never transferred.\n\nExample 2, exact case-17 shape. Caller places are 0 and 1; callee places are 2 (local L), 3 (value v) and 4 (carrier).\n- `TransferStep K0 4 1 [2] h0 (.ok h1)`: L's root goes along with the carrier.\n- `DependStep 3 2 h1 (.ok h2)`.\n- `TransferStep K0 3 0 [] h2 (.ok h3)`.\n- `ExitStep h3 (.ok (exitEff h3))`.\n- After exit: `(exitEff h3).D 0 = [2] ∧ (exitEff h3).afp 2 = [2] ∧ ¬ (exitEff h3).Usable 2`.\nThe same sequence without the carrier is `.reject`, which is the report's case-17 verdict.\n\nThe theorems dependent_cannot_escape_frame and exitFrame_releases_all hold only because 'held by f' is the rewritable `frame` field. Report (c) 12, (c) 13 and (e) 4 note that `auths` is a free argument, but never this consequence.",
    "fix": "Report this as a question for arbitration: locality of an anchor and of an authority must not follow the rewritable holder frame. For example, a root authority's locality should be the frame of the place it roots, and ExitPre should reject a surviving active root authority whose footprint lies in the exiting frame. Until then, restrict `auths` or list the gap in (d) and (e)."
   },
   {
    "title": "`arena.issue` installs a dependency into `dst` with no non-escape check (MM-03.3.6). `depend` rejects the same anchor and destination.",
    "severity": "major",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean IssuePre l.1884-1891 (only `s.Usable dst` constrains dst); issueEff l.1903 `D := fun q => if q = dst then s.D dst ++ [via] else s.D q`",
    "cause": "formalization error",
    "evidence": "Spec MM-03.3.6: « Une valeur dépendante ne peut être installée dans une destination dont le cadre survivrait à celui d'une ancre locale dont elle dépend. »\n\nThe report applies this restriction only to O4.6 and O5.5 ((c) 13). (c) 7 lists only Usable for issue's destination. No section mentions omitting it for issue.\n\nCheck (scratch Fid.lean, all `by decide`). Setup: f2a has the caller place 0 (frame 1) and, in the callee (frame 2), arena metadata 1 and storage 2 with leaves 3 and 4. ar2 = ⟨1,[3,4],[3,4],[],2⟩.\n- Root authority 1 has origin `none` and is held by frame 2.\n- `IssueStep KA ar2 1 [3] 0 f2a (.ok …)` holds, with `(issueEff f2a ar2 1 [3] 0).1.D 0 = [1]`.\n- `DependStep 0 1 f2a .reject` holds.\n\nSo the caller value is anchored on a local root anchor of the younger frame. The escape is caught only later: `ExitStep (issueEff …).1 .reject`.",
    "fix": "Add `NoEscape s via (placeFrame s.P dst)` to IssuePre, or list the omission in (c) or (e)."
   },
   {
    "title": "`arena.issue` writes `dst` (sets it to Init and changes its dependencies) with no access right. It bypasses an exclusive Modify held by another authority, and it has no 'can receive' check.",
    "severity": "major",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean issueEff l.1902 `I := fun l => if l ∈ footprint s.P dst then .init else s.I l`; IssuePre l.1884-1891",
    "cause": "formalization error",
    "evidence": "Spec §5 canWrite3: « Une autorité effective de modification couvre les feuilles concernées. Aucune autorité ordinaire incompatible n'exerce de droit effectif sur ces feuilles. » and I1 (Modify/Modify and Modify/Observe incompatible).\n\n`transfer` at least requires dst to have no Init leaf (O4.2 reading, (c) 12). issue checks nothing on dst beyond Usable.\n\nCheck (scratch Fid.lean, `by decide`). f3a has places 0 (metadata), 1 (storage, leaves 2 and 3) and 4 (dst). f3b = `deriveEff f3a 2 4 .modify`, so authority 3 holds `effective f3b 3 4 = some .modify` and the root has `effective f3b 2 4 = none`.\n- `IssueStep KA ar3 0 [2] 4 f3b (.ok …)` holds.\n- The resulting state has `I 4 = .init`, while `f3b.I 4 = .uninit`.\n- `Write3Step 2 [4] f3b .reject` holds.\n\nSo issue performs the write3Eff effect on a leaf where another authority has exclusive effective Modify. (c) 17 introduces `dst` but does not state that it is written without authority. (e) 2 raises the no-rights question only for transfer and read/write.",
    "fix": "Require on `dst` the same reception and write conditions as transfer or canWrite3, or list this in (c) or (e)."
   },
   {
    "title": "The reset effect never realises the `Invalidates` invalidation, so I3 does not govern reset (arbitrage 3), and `arena_reset_rejects_live_dependents_underInv` only restates a ResetPre clause.",
    "severity": "minor",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean ResetPre l.1916-1918, resetEff l.1926-1927 `(s, { ar with available := ar.storage, issued := [] })`, ArenaResetContract l.2037-2038, theorem l.2043-2048",
    "cause": "formalization error",
    "evidence": "Arbitrage 3: « reset est une opération Invalidates gouvernée par I3 ». Spec §6 effects: « Invalidation des anciennes émissions selon le contrat de l'arène. » Spec §10: « Une preuve qui réénonce directement une précondition comme conclusion ne constitue pas, à elle seule, une validation suffisante du mécanisme. »\n\nresetEff leaves S3 unchanged. Check: `(resetEff f2a ar2).1 = f2a := rfl`. So an anchor that `Invalidates` (and ArenaResetContract: « reset invalide l'ancre de l'arène et toute autorité qui en dérive ») declares invalidated stays active, which means valid under arbitrage 2.\n\nAs a result, I3 is preserved by reset whether or not ResetPre's second clause holds. The theorem's proof is literally `.reject fun h => h.2 q ?_ hq x hx (hk x hxa)`, a direct application of that clause. Report (h) presents it as a K-conditioned theorem and does not say it restates a precondition.",
    "fix": "Either model invalidation in resetEff, or state in the report ((d) or (e)) that I3 does not govern reset in this model and that the theorem restates ResetPre."
   },
   {
    "title": "The §5 canWrite3 clause « L'écriture ne doit pas implicitement invalider une valeur dépendante encore utilisable » is neither formalised nor listed.",
    "severity": "minor",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean canWrite3 l.601-606 and its docstring; report (b)",
    "cause": "missing coverage",
    "evidence": "Spec §5: « L'écriture ne doit pas implicitement invalider une valeur dépendante encore utilisable. »\n\nThe canWrite3 docstring lists only the Modify, exclusivity and DepsValid conditions, plus the omitted type condition.\n\n`grep -nE 'implicitement' formal/reports/MM03_v0.1.md` returns nothing. Report (b) lists the other dropped or by-construction clauses (O1.5, O4.3, O5.3, the §5 type clause) but not this one. In the model it holds only vacuously, because write3 never changes activity; that reading is not stated either.",
    "fix": "Add it to (b) as holding by construction, with the reason, or raise it in (e)."
   },
   {
    "title": "EnterPre adds an unlisted precondition: the parent of a new local must be a preceding new local.",
    "severity": "minor",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean EnterPre l.516-518 `OptP ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)) (fun r => s.P.length ≤ r ∧ r < s.P.length + i) True`",
    "cause": "report error",
    "evidence": "Spec O6 preconditions: « Le cadre appelant est actif. Les arguments transmis respectent leurs conditions d'accès et de transfert. » Neither constrains the parent of a local.\n\nCheck (scratch Fid.lean): `EnterStep [(some 0, 0)] (enterEff S3.init [(none, 0)]) .reject` holds by `decide`.\n\nReport (c) 5 says only that places are created by enterFrame. No (c) entry gives this rejection condition or the sentence it rests on. The task requires every decision not dictated by the text to appear in (c).",
    "fix": "Add a (c) entry. It keeps existing leaves as leaves, so authority footprints stay leaf sets; say so as the justification."
   }
  ]

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

# AGENTS.md

Claude Code implements. Codex reviews. Both follow this file.

## Source of truth

- `specs/` is normative and the only source of semantics. Before acting, read the spec text the task depends on. Never rely on memory, summaries, comments or earlier sessions.
- Never restate spec content in code comments or agent files. Point to its location.
- Spec beats code. If the spec is ambiguous, contradictory or silent on something the task needs: stop and report the exact passage with a concrete example of the problem. Never pick an interpretation yourself.
- Representation choices (structure or inductive type, function or relation) are yours when they change no accepted program and no behavior. A choice that does is a semantic question: stop and report.

## Scope

- Do exactly the task. No unrequested features, generalization, refactoring or "robustness" additions. Put suggestions in the report.
- Do not edit `specs/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `formal/DESIGN.md` unless the task says so.

## Lean

- The Lake project is in `formal/`. `formal/DESIGN.md` governs how to formalize, never what the semantics is. Propose design decisions it does not settle in your report; never take them silently.
- Every definition or theorem that encodes a spec rule cites the rule's location in its docstring.
- A definition says what its rule says. Never make a definition more permissive, add an unjustified hypothesis or narrow a theorem's domain to obtain a proof.
- Never change a theorem statement, or a definition it depends on, to make a proof go through. If stuck, stop and report the goal state.
- Never use `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom` or `native_decide`.
- Every `.lean` file under `formal/` is part of the build target.
- Done means:
  - `lake build` (in `formal/`) succeeds;
  - this prints nothing: `grep -rnE '\b(sorry|admit|native_decide)\b|^\s*axiom\b' --include='*.lean' --exclude-dir=.lake .`
  - for each theorem completed by the task, `#print axioms` lists nothing beyond `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.

## Report

Spec passages implemented (by location), what changed, what is unproven or open, spec problems found.

## Review (Codex)

Adversarial and read-only. For each change, check:

- It says exactly what the spec says: not stronger, not weaker. Read definitions, hypotheses and quantifiers, not only proofs. A theorem that holds because a definition is too permissive or its hypotheses are unsatisfiable is blocking.
- Each formalized rule cites its spec location.
- No theorem statement or dependency was changed without the task allowing it.
- No interpretation was chosen silently where the spec is unclear.
- Nothing outside the task was added.

When a milestone is declared complete, compare the rules in its announced scope with the spec locations cited in `formal/`, and list every rule left without a definition or theorem.

Every finding needs evidence: a spec quote, a counterexample or command output. No evidence, no finding. Never ask for additions beyond the task.

Output: verdict (block / changes / ok), then each finding with severity, location, cause (formalization error, missing coverage or spec defect) and evidence.
- [ERN formal exploratory passes](ern-formal-mm02-exploration.md) — French briefs, MM-02 branch, reports/ never merged, spec outside repo
